headline: Most people listen to respond, not to understand
universal_truth: True listening is one of the rarest and most valuable gifts we can give
fun_facts: Studies show we remember only 25-50% of what we hear—and less when we're planning our response
Active listening can reduce misunderstandings by up to 80% in workplace settings
The average person speaks at 125 words per minute, but we can process 400—leaving room for distraction
discussion_questions: Who in your life makes you feel truly heard?
What stops you from listening fully?
How does it feel when someone really listens to you?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Here's a test: in your last conversation, were you really listening—or were you waiting for your turn to talk? Most of us are thinking about what we'll say next while others are still speaking. Today, we learn why that's a problem and how to fix it.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: We speak at about 125 words per minute, but our brains can process 400. That gap is where our attention wanders—to our phones, our to-do list, our brilliant comeback. How do great listeners stay present?
cliff.prompt: What's the key to truly listening?

options.response: Exactly. Listening to understand, rather than to reply, changes everything.

options.text: Don't interrupt and maintain eye contact
options.response: Those help, but there's something deeper...

q1.title: The Retention Problem
q1.script: Immediately after a conversation, we remember only 50% of what was said. After 48 hours? Just 25%. And that's when we're trying. When we're planning our response while others speak, retention drops even further. Listening takes intention.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "The Retention Problem"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: The Gap That Wanders
q2.script: We process speech 3 times faster than people can talk. That cognitive surplus should help us think deeper about what we're hearing. Instead, our minds drift to distractions. Great listeners use that gap to seek understanding, not escape.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: The Power of Being Heard
q3.script: When people feel truly listened to, their stress hormones decrease and they become more creative and collaborative. Listening isn't just nice—it changes the speaker's brain chemistry. Your attention is a gift with real effects.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Listening is not waiting. It's not silence while you prepare to speak. Real listening is putting aside your own agenda and genuinely seeking to understand another human being. It's surprisingly rare—and surprisingly powerful.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 10—our first ten days complete. Thank you for listening to me. Tomorrow, we begin a new chapter. Until then, practice the gift of your full attention.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Full Presence - Listening Practice
growTrack.learning_objective: Develop the skill of listening without planning a response
growTrack.activity: In one conversation today, practice this: After the other person finishes speaking, count to 2 in your head before responding. Use that pause to make sure you understood, not to prepare your reply.
